extracted.intended_audience: plain TeX users, macro writers, and typesetters learning register/box/insertion management and math typing
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance from The TeXbook on using numeric and box registers, allocation conventions, insertions and page-breaking, and on typing mathematics (math mode, scripts, roots, spacing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Register-definition primitives
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands like \countdef, \dimendef, \skipdef and \muskipdef create control sequences that act as aliases for numeric registers (e.g. no is an abbreviation for \count28).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After a control sequence has been defined by \countdef it can be used in TeX commands exactly as if it were an integer parameter like \tolerance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box register allocation and use
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX has 256 box registers \box0 to \box255; assign a box with \setbox<number>=<box> (e.g., \setbox3=\hbox{A}) and inspect dimensions with \wd<number>, \ht<number>, \dp<number>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Box registers are local to groups. Use \unhbox/\unvbox to remove one level of boxing; use \copy/\unhcopy/\unvcopy to preserve box contents when desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boxes are consumed when used
rubrics_metrics.description: Using \box<number> removes (voids) the contents of that box register (TeX does this for efficiency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want to use a box without wiping out its contents, use \copy<number> instead of \box<number> (e.g., \raise2pt\copy3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unboxing removes outer-level glue only
rubrics_metrics.description: An unboxing operation (\unhbox/\unvbox) 'unsets' any glue that was set at the box's outer level; glue inside nested boxes is not affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \setbox5=\hbox{A \hbox{B C}}; \setbox6=\hbox to 1.05\wd5{\unhcopy5} makes \box6 five percent wider than \box5 by stretching the outer glue but not inner-hbox glue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Void register vs empty box
rubrics_metrics.description: A register that is 'void' is different from one that contains an empty box (height, width and depth zero); allowed operations differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If \box3 is void you can say \unhbox3, \unvbox3, \unhcopy3 or \unvcopy3; if \box3 equals \hbox{} you can say only \unhbox3 or \unhcopy3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid deep nested boxes; build by accretion
rubrics_metrics.description: When constructing large boxes (e.g., a table of contents), prefer using \unhbox or \unvbox to accrete material rather than nesting boxes inside boxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nesting deeply can use more memory and may exceed hardware or software limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \show* diagnostics to inspect registers
rubrics_metrics.description: You can experiment and inspect register contents with \show commands, e.g. \showthe\count1, \showthe\dimen2, \showthe\skip3, and \showbox4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Box contents appear in the log file unless \tracingonline=1. Plain TeX provides \tracingall to turn on every interaction mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation conventions: use \new... to reserve registers
rubrics_metrics.description:
To avoid conflicts between macros, use allocation primitives like 
ewcount, 
ewdimen, 
ewskip, 
ewmuskip, 
ewbox, etc., which assign a unique underlying register and define a control sequence via \countdef or \chardef.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format macros can then use names (e.g., \exno) without knowing exact register numbers; see Appendices for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserved scratch registers and special registers
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain TeX reserves certain registers for scratchwork: \count255, \dimen255, \skip255, \muskip255, and \dimen0..\dimen9, \skip0..\skip9, \muskip0..9, \box0..\box9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using special registers like \count0..\count9 and \box255 unless you know what you are doing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal register use within groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Any register can be used for short-term storage inside a group (including ordinarily reserved registers) because register changes are local to groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure TeX will not output pages before the group ends, since output routines invoked prematurely may cause conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Times when an output routine may be invoked
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX may invoke an output routine whenever it tries to move something from 'recent contributions' to the 'current page'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: (a) at the beginning or end of a paragraph in the main vertical list; (b) at the beginning or end of a displayed equation within such a paragraph; (c) after completing an \halign in vertical mode; (d) after contributing a box/penalty/insertion to the main vertical list; (e) after an output routine has ended. Avoid dangerous register usage across these points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insertion classes and their tied registers
rubrics_metrics.description: There are 255 classes of insertions \insert0..\insert254; each class n is tied to \box n, \count n, \dimen n and \skip n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain TeX defines \newinsert\footins to allocate footnote insertions (e.g., \box\footins holds footnote material); floating top inserts use a separate class, e.g., \newinsert\topins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semantics of \box n, \count n, \dimen n, \skip n for insertions
rubrics_metrics.description: For insertion class n: \box n is where the material appears when a page is output; \count n is the magnification factor for page breaking; \dimen n is the maximum insertion size per page; \skip n is the extra space to allocate on a page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \count\footins=1000 (one-to-one relationship), in double columns use 500, and for marginal notes something like zero; \skip\footins=\bigskipamount adds extra space before footnotes on a page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit insertion size per page with \dimen\<insert>
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \dimen\<insert> to cap how much material of that insertion class may accumulate on a single page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain TeX sets \dimen\footins=8in so that a page shouldn't consist entirely of footnotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insertion/page-goal magnification factor (\count n)
rubrics_metrics.description: \count n is 1000 times the factor by which the natural height-plus-depth x of an insertion affects the page goal (y) when estimating page-breaking costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No actual magnification is performed; \count n is bookkeeping. Choose values appropriate to layout (e.g., 1000 for one-column footnotes, 500 for double-column footnotes).

rubrics_metrics.name: High-level insertion page-breaking algorithm (steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: When moving an \insert n to the current page TeX follows an algorithm: adjust page goal y by outer glue and previous insertions; if previous insertion split then add \floatingpenalty; test if insertion fits without splitting (check \dimen n and t+d+xf - z <= y); if not, tentatively split the insertion and compute least-cost split using a page-breaking-like algorithm, adjust y by nf and increase q by penalty r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalties of -10000 make splits very attractive; floating behavior is achieved by small initial penalties and \floatingpenalty=0 for floating top inserts; non-floating insertions use larger split penalties to discourage splitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Splitting insertions with \vsplit
rubrics_metrics.description: \vsplit<number> to <dimen> produces a vbox obtained by splitting off specified amount from a box register; it finds the least-cost break assuming a goal height, using \splitmaxdepth and \splittopskip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If optimum break is at end of list an implicit \penalty-10000 is assumed to ensure legality; \vsplit prunes discardable items after break and if nothing remains original box may become void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not change key insertion parameters during contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't change \box n, \count n, \dimen n or \skip n while TeX is contributing insertions to the current page because the algorithm assumes they are static.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may change \floatingpenalty, \splittopskip, and \splitmaxdepth; TeX uses values that were current just inside the closing brace of the \insert group when splitting/floating insertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using penalties to control splitting and floating
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties influence split attractiveness and floating: negative large penalties favor splits; \floatingpenalty is added if a previous insertion has been split, affecting the accumulated insertion penalties for the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix B uses \floatingpenalty=20000 in footnote insertions to discourage footnote splits before others can start, but \floatingpenalty=0 in floating topinserts.

rubrics_metrics.name: How \footnote insertion ties to page and reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The \footnote macro inserts into the horizontal list of a paragraph; after line breaking this insertion moves into the vertical list immediately after the line that contained it, and therefore is placed on the page that contains its reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because there is no legal breakpoint between the line and the insertion, TeX will put the insertion on the same page as the line that contains it.

rubrics_metrics.name: What happens when best page break is chosen
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX removes everything after the chosen breakpoint from the bottom of the current page and puts it back at top of recent contributions; the breakpoint is placed at top of recent contributions, output penalty recorded in \outputpenalty, and remaining insertions are classified and processed into \box255 and other places for the output routine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsplit insertions are appended to \box<insert class>, split insertions are handled via the previously computed split, and held-over insertions are placed separately; output routine assembles final pages from \box255 and insertion boxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \new... and \chardef for named boxes/controls
rubrics_metrics.description: When you do \newbox\abstract TeX allocates a box register (e.g., \box45) and defines \abstract by saying \chardef\abstract=45 so that you can use \box\abstract and \copy\abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no \boxdef primitive; allocation macros hide actual register numbers from macro writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \math mode delimiters and basic spacing conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Enclose math in $...$ (inline) or $$...$$ (display); letters become italic, digits and punctuation remain roman; TeX ignores spaces between $'s, and handles math spacing automatically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can type spaces freely around operators; TeX supplies appropriate spacing but control sequences exist to override spacing if needed (see Chapter 18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Superscript/subscript syntax rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ^ for superscripts and _ for subscripts; they apply only to the next single character unless grouped in braces to form a subformula. Double superscripts/subscripts without grouping are illegal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multiple-token scripts use {...}. Examples: x^{2y}, y_{x_2}. Empty scripts are parsed as empty subformulas — prefer explicit braces (e.g., {}_2F_3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering and alignment of simultaneous scripts
rubrics_metrics.description: You may have simultaneous subscript and superscript in either order (e.g., x^2_3 or x_3^2); they are positioned over each other and some letters slightly 'tuck in' subscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want left edges aligned, insert a null subformula: P{}_{2}^{-2} trick to align edges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of \prime and quote shorthand
rubrics_metrics.description: \prime stands for the prime symbol (used mainly in superscripts); plain TeX provides shorthand: ' instead of \prime and '' instead of \prime\prime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because \prime is treated as a large symbol, TeX expects it primarily in superscripts rather than pre-shifted small prime glyphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roots, overlines, underlines and consistent vertical alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \sqrt, \root ... \of, \overline and \underline; these adjust bar lengths/positions according to the size of the subformula. To get uniform vertical position across different radicals use \mathstrut.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: \mathstrut is an invisible zero-width box with height/depth equal to a parenthesis, making subformulas containing it have the same height/depth; \smash and \phantom (Chapter 18) provide more control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character classes in math mode
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters A..Z and a..z denote italic 'ordinary symbols' (variables). The 18 characters 0..9 and a set of punctuation remain ordinary but in roman; digits and punctuation do not get extra math spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between the letter 'o' and the numeral '0' in contexts like O(n); use appropriate characters (e.g., type x_O instead of x_o when O(...) is intended).

rubrics_metrics.name: Braces for subformulas and grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: Braces serve to delimit subformulas and group tokens so that operations like scripts and overlines apply to the grouped subformula as a single object; TeX makes a box for each subformula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer the simpler, natural grouping where it matches mathematical intent; use grouping to avoid double-script errors or ambiguous application.
